reference: The 2022 Health of Women and Children Report includes measures across multiple domains such as Community and Family Safety (e.g., Child Victimization, Firearm Deaths), Economic Resources (e.g., Children in Poverty, Food Insecurity), Education (e.g., Early Childhood Education, High School Graduation), Social Support and Engagement (e.g., Adverse Childhood Experiences, Foster Care Instability), Clinical Care (e.g., Adequate Prenatal Care, Cervical Cancer Screening), Nutrition and Physical Activity (e.g., Exercise, Fruit and Vegetable Consumption), Sexual Health (e.g., Chlamydia, Unintended Pregnancy), Behavioral Health (e.g., Drug Deaths, Postpartum Depression), Mortality (e.g., Maternal Mortality, Infant Mortality), and Physical Health (e.g., Obesity, High Blood Pressure). These measures collectively assess the health outcomes, behaviors, and social determinants affecting women and children.
